critical_code_review_comments: routes/calls.py L237-266 decline_call: The `answered_elsewhere` short-circuit lets the caller themselves declining their own call also mark it answered — because the check `p.get('id') != call.get('started_by')` won't match the caller. That's actually the desired UX (caller cancelling shouldn't drop a missed card on themselves), but it also means: if the CALLER hits /decline on their own outgoing ring, no missed card is ever posted and no unring is broadcast to callees. Not a bug for the current flows (banner is only shown to callees), just worth documenting.

routes/calls.py L249: `manager.send_to_user(current['id'], call_unring)` only stops the ring on the DECLINER's own devices. Other callees on the same ring keep hearing it until their own timeout/decline fires — which matches the 'per-user' decline semantics documented in the docstring, but means a 3-way group ring will keep ringing device B for another ~30s after A declines. Consider a workspace-scoped ring-stop when the CALLER cancels; today the caller cancel path is `POST /calls/{id}/end` which does broadcast call_unring to all members (L226-228), so this is fine — just note the asymmetry between decline (per-user) and cancel (all-members).

services/calls_runtime.post_missed_call_card L109-110: `from_name = call.get('started_by_name') or 'Someone'`. If a caller ever renames themselves between start_call and decline, the missed card retains the OLD name (a stale name at the time of ring start). Minor cosmetic drift.

CallRingListener.tsx L49-52 declineCall: swallows API errors (`.catch(() => {})`). If /api/calls/{id}/decline returns 5xx (e.g. call already ended after cleanup), the banner still dismisses locally so UX is fine — but note that no telemetry surfaces server-side decline failures.

CallRecapCard.tsx L27-41 addTask: no error visibility. On failure we silently reset the button (delete state[i]). If tasks POST returns 4xx (e.g. rate-limited, permission denied), the user just sees the button revert with no toast. Consider surfacing an error state (e.g. `state='error'` with red 'Retry' label).

chat/[id].tsx L735 onPress={() => startCall(callMode)} on 'Call back': starts a brand-new call. That matches the product spec, but the missed card's own call_id (md.call_id) references the ORIGINAL declined call. If the user taps Call back multiple times in quick succession without a network, we may create multiple simultaneous /calls/start POSTs. `startCall` should ideally guard on an in-flight ref (or debounce).

team.tsx L303 gating: `timelineFor.status === 'invited' || timelineFor.must_change_password` correctly hides Resend for joined users. Consider also hiding it when the current user is viewing their OWN row — technically owner could 'resend' themselves an invite (harmless but confusing). Minor UX polish.

Playwright note (unchanged from iter 133): Animated.View with SlideInUp on incoming-call-banner still refuses native click during the slide-in transform. Use page.evaluate JS click for automated tests until the outer wrapper is split from the transform.
